full_judgment:
SK Sinha J: Almost identical facts and common law points involve in these Rules and accordingly, these Rules are disposed of by this judgment. Accused Sarwar M Kamal obtained Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1587 of 2002 for quashing the proceedings in CR No. 698 of 2001 pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. Accused Sarwar M Kamal obtained another Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1589 of 2002 for quashing the proceedings in CR Case No. 753 of 2001 pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. Accused Mominul Islam Khan obtained Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9877 of 2002 for quashing the proceedings in CR Case No. 132 of 2001 pending in the Court of Magistrate, 1st Class, Court No. 1, Nilphamari and accused Biplob Samadder obtained Rule in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7016 of 2003 for quashing the proceedings in CR Case No. 469 of 2003 pending in the Court of Metropolitan Magistrate, Dhaka. 

 2. The question that arises for consideration in these Rules is whether the payee or, as the case may be, the holder in due course of a dishonoured cheque can validly initiate prosecution against the drawer of the cheque for an offence under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 with reference to the dishonour if he has not taken advantage of initiating prosecution of the first dishonour either at his own volition or on the request of the drawer. In the alternative, whether if the payee or the holder of the cheque in due course fails to initiate prosecution on the first dishonour of the cheque, he will forfeit his right to do so on the basis of the second or any subsequent dishonour of the cheque. 

 3. It is contended on behalf of the petitioners that if a cheque is dishonoured due to insufficiency of funds in the account, a prosecution under section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act can be instituted but if the payee or the holder of the cheque fails to initiate prosecution after such dishonour on any of the grounds and presents the cheque again for encashment after some time at the request of the drawer or on his own volition in expectation that it will be encashed, he will forfeit his right to prosecute the drawer on the basis of the second or any subsequent dishonour of the cheque. References have been made in support of their contention in the cases of Abdus Salam vs Md Munshi Rashed Kamal and another, 54 DLR 234 and SM Anwar Hossain vs Md Shafiul Alam (Chand) and another 51 DLR (AD) 218. The question that falls for our consideration is whether a prosecution under section 138 of the Negotiable, Instruments Act can be initiated against the drawer of the cheque on the basis of the second or any subsequent dishonour of the cheque if the dishonoured cheque is presented for encashment after some time at the request of the drawer. At the outset we may point out that there is conflict of opinion on the point between two Benches of this Court. Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act reads as follows: 

 (b) the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for the payment of the said amount of money by giving a notice, in writing, to the drawer of the cheque, within fifteen days of the receipt of information by him from the bank regarding the return of the cheque as unpaid, and 

 (c) the drawer of such cheque fails to make the payment of the said amount of money to the payee or, as the case may be, to the holder in due course of the cheque within fifteen days of the receipt of the said notice. 

 5. Where a statute does not consist merely of one enactment but contains a number of different provisions regulating the manner in which something is to be done, it often happens that some of these provisions are to be treated as being directory only while others are to be considered absolute and essential, that is to say, some of the provisions may be disregarded without rendering invalid the thing to be done but others not. (Craies on Statute Law, Seventh Edition, pages 266-267). The payee may resort to clause (b) of the proviso by serving notice demanding for payment of the said amount of money if he decides to prosecute the drawer of the cheque or he may wait for some time on the request of the drawer. After service of notice as above, if the drawer of the cheque fails to make the payment within 15(fifteen) days on the receipt of the notice, the cause of action for filing a criminal case arises. The next question is, when a dishonoured cheque gives rise to the institution of a complaint under section 141 of the Act, which reads: 

 (a) No Court shall take cognizance of any offence punishable under section 138 except upon a complaint, in writing, made by the payee or, as the case may be, the holder in due course of the cheque; 

 6. The offence created by the Act is made cognisable only on the basis of a written complaint made by the payee or the holder in due course of the cheque and that too in case such complaint is made within one month of the date on which the cause of action arises. Clause (b) of section 141 clearly provides that no Court shall take cognizance of the offence unless a complaint is made within the period of limitation after constituting the cause of action. Now the question is, when a cause of action for filing a complaint under the proviso to clause (b) arises. 

 7. Suffice it to mention that the language used in sections 138 and 142 of the Indian enactment, the Banking Public Financial Institutions and Negotiable Instruments Laws (Amendment) Act, 1988 and those of ours in sections 138 and 141 are in pari materia. There were conflicting views in different High Courts in India as to when a cause of action for initiation of a criminal prosecution under section 138 of the Act would arise. In the case of Mahadevan Sunil Kumar vs Bhadan 1991 (1) Ker LT 651, it has been observed "the cause of action for filing the complaint may arise on several occasions and the payee or holder in due course is entitled to present the cheque at any time within a period of 6 months from the date at which it was drawn and if other conditions are fulfilled he can launch a complaint on the basis of the second or any subsequent dishonour of the cheque as the cheque would remain valid for a period of 6 months. “The High Courts of Bombay, Kolkatta, Andhra Pradesh and Madras have concurred on the said views. In the case of Kumaresan vs Ameerrappa 1991(1) Ker LT 893 a contrary view was taken. It has been observed: "there can only be one cause of action as far as a particular cheque is concerned for the purpose of section 138 of the Act." The Punjab and Haryana High Courts have followed this view. A Full Bench of Kerala High Court in the case of Messrs SKD Lakshmanan Fireworks Industries and another vs KV Sivarama Krishna and another, 1995 Cri LJ 1384 (FB) considered the said decisions and approved the views taken in the case of Mahadevan Sunil Kumar. The Bench observed: 

 8. The Supreme Court of India in Sadanandan Vhadran vs Madhavan Sunil Kumar, AIR 1998 (AC) 3043 did not approve the views taken in Messrs SKD Lakshmanan Fireworks Industries' case and observed, in generic sense, the expression 'cause of action' means every fact which it is necessary to establish to support a right or obtain a judgment but clause (b) of section 142 gives it a restrictive meaning, "it refers to only one fact which will give rise to the cause of action and that is the failure to make the payment within 15 days from the date of the receipt of the notice" MK Mukharjee, J speaking for the Supreme Court, observed: "On each presentation of the cheque and its dishonour a fresh right and not cause of action accrues in his favour. He may, therefore, without taking pre-emptory action in exercise of his right under clause (b) section 138, go on presenting the cheque so as to enable him to exercise such right at any point of time during the validity of the cheque. But, once he gives a notice under clause (b) of section 138 he forfeits such right, for, in case of failure of the drawer to pay the money within the stipulated time he would be liable for the offence and the cause of action for filing the complaint will arise." Our Appellate Division expressed similar views in the case of SM Anwar Hossain (supra). It was observed: 

 9. It is true that in the said reported case the cheque was not dishonoured on repeated occasions but the Appellate Division on consideration of the relevant provisions addressed the point as to when a right of a payee to prosecute the drawer would accrue and when his right would be forfeited. The object of incorporating sections 138, 139, 140 and 141 in place of sections 138 and 139 in Chapter XVII of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881 by Act XIX of 1994 is to enable the payee or the holder in due course to avail criminal remedy in case of bouncing of the cheque for insufficiency of funds in the account subject to certain strict conditions. Facts which give rise to prosecution of a person under section 138 are that (a) the cheque drawn for payment of money for liquidation of liability has been dishonoured by the bank; (b) the cheque has been presented within the prescribed period; (c) the payee or the holder of the cheque, as the case may be, makes a demand for payment by giving a notice to the drawer within the stipulated period, and (d) the drawer fails to make payment within the prescribed period. 

 10. The expression "Cause of Action" according to PG Osborne, Law Dictionary means "The fact or combination of facts which give rise to a right of action." In terms of clause (b) of section 141 a 'cause of action' for prosecution under section 13,8 arises if the drawer fails to make the payment within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice served under clause (b) of section 138. The Apex Courts of Bangladesh and India have taken uniform view that if the drawer fails to make the payment within fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice served under section 138(b), a 'cause of action' for initiation of a criminal prosecution will arise. If the bank on any ground dishonours a cheque, no cause of action to prosecute the drawer arises unless the payee serves a notice demanding for payment in accordance with clause (b) of section 138 upon him. In other words, it may be said that the aggrieved person does not acquire a right of launching a complaint in terms of clause (b) of section 141 on the dishonour of the cheque unless other conditions are satisfied. If that be so, there can be no bar on the part of the payee or holder in due course to present the cheque for encashment on repeated occasions during the validity of the cheque, either on the request of the drawer or at his own volition, without exercising his right to prosecute the drawer on complying with formalities on the basis of the first dishonour of the cheque. This dishonour of the cheque does not forfeit his right to prosecute the drawer if the cheque is presented within the period of its validity. The only bar is that once the cause of action arises, the limitation for filing the complaint will be reckoned from the day following the day on which the period of fifteen days from the date of receipt of the notice and if no complaint is filed within the period of one month, he forfeits his right. The Court has no power to extend the period of limitation even if the payee shows genuine cause. In this regard the Appellate Division in SM Anwar Hossain's case observed, "The subsequent allegation will not save the limitation." The Appellate Division in SM Anwar Hossain's case has settled the law point leaving no stone unturned and unless it is modified or statutorily changed, it is the last word on the subject. 

 11. Now let us consider some decisions of this Court on this point. In the case of Nazrul Islam Mallik vs Tofazzal Hossain 8 BLC 443 a Division Bench of this Court following a decision of the Appellate Division in Habibur Rahman Howlader vs State and another, 53 DLR (AD) 111, observed, the decision of the Appellate Division is that a payee of the cheque can present it for as many times as he wishes to the bank for encashment within the period of validity and it is the option of the payee to decide at what point of time he could initiate the proceeding." We fully agree with the views that a cheque can be presented on repeated occasions for encashment within the period of validity but with due respect, we reserve our opinion regarding some observations made in the reported case. It was observed: "the matter has been finally decided by the Appellate Division in Howlader's case as reported in 53 DLR (AD) 111." In that case the Appellate Division did not give any decision on interpretation of sections 138 and 141 of the Act and dismissed the leave petition summarily by a succinct order that could not be said that the law point was finally settled in that case. "Finality" to a judgment or order may be said to have been given only in those cases, which decided the dispute which arose in the appeal on merit after hearing both parties. In general, a judgment, which determines the principal matter in question, both on facts and law, is termed as 'final'. In the case of Hasibul Bashar (Md) vs Dilshed Huda and another, 55 DLR 200, another Division Bench of this Court though SM Anwar Hossain's case was referred to for consideration but the said Division Bench refrained from making any observation on merit on the reasoning that the accused would be able to get opportunity to raise the point at the time of framing charge. However, in the case of Abdus Salam (supra), another Division Bench of this Court on following SM Anwar Hossain's case quashed the proceedings. In that case the cheque was dishonoured for the fourth time during the validity of the cheque and thereafter the complaint was filed after compliance of formalities. The Division Bench held that the complaint was barred by limitation. With due respect, the said Bench, failed to appreciate the ratio decidendi of the decision of SM Anwar Hossain's case. Abdus Salam's case may be ignored as it is in conflict with SM Anwar Hossain's case. 

 12. Bearing these principles in mind, let us look at the facts of these cases. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 7016 of 2003, the cheque was lastly dishonoured on 15-1-2003 and a notice was served for payment of the amount upon the accused-petitioner on 22-1-2003, which was received by him on 11-2-2003, and the complaint was made on 18-2-2003. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 9877 of 2002, the cheque was lastly dishonoured on 5-7-2001 and thereupon a registered notice upon the accused-petitioner was served on 15-7-2001 and the complaint was made on 7-8-2001. In Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 1587 of 2002, the cheque was dishonoured on 22-4-2001 and the legal notice for payment was served upon the accused-petitioner on 24-4-2001, which was received by the accused on 29-4-2001 and 30-4-2001 and thereafter the complaint was made on 27-5-2001. In Criminal Miscellaneous Cases Nos. 1587 of 2002 and 1589 of 2002, the cheques were dishonoured on 22-4-2001 and the legal notices were served on 24-4-2001, which were received by the accused on 29-4-2001 and 30-4-2001, and the complaints were made on 10-6-2001. In all these cases, the notices were served demanding for payment of the money within 15 (fifteen) days of the date of the last dishonour of the cheques and that the complaint petitions were filed within 1(one) month of the date on which the cause of action arises under clause (c) of the proviso to section 138 of the Act. Therefore, we find the complaints were made within statutory period of limitation as provided in clause (b) of section 141 of the Negotiable Instruments Act. The learned Magistrate, in the premises, have committed no error of law in taking cognizance of the offence. The proceedings were legally initiated in accordance with law and the learned Magistrates were justified in taking cognizance of offence against the accused-petitioners. In that view of the matter, we find no substance in the contention of the learned Advocates for the petitioners. We find no merit in these Rules.
